messages:
marie: FYI customer AcmeCorp reporting a spike of 503s for hosted inference since ~03:45 UTC, they see auth failures in logs.
marie: sample from their SDK logs: `HTTP/1.1 503 Service Unavailable` and repeated retry loops.
kevin: they pasted a correlation id, 3f2a1b. attaching network traces from their side.
marie: internal logs show a lot of timeouts talking to the keystore service: 
```
2026-03-18T03:46:12Z auth-service WARN keystore request failed: dial tcp 10.12.8.9:443: i/o timeout
2026-03-18T03:46:12Z auth-service ERROR token_signer: failed to sign claim: keystore timeout
2026-03-18T03:46:13Z gateway INFO proxy upstream returned 503 for request id=3f2a1b
```
marie: customer notes they were on v1.8.2 of our SDK and saw p95 latency jump from 120ms to 1.4s before 503s start.
raj: looking at infra metrics now. keystore cluster shows connection spikes and many 5xx from the keystore pods.
raj: also seeing increased egress NAT exhaustion in the region (US-W). possible culprits: keystore pool exhaustion or external KMS throttling.
olivia: can we confirm if this is our internal keystore (keystore-service) or external KMS? logs show internal IP so likely our keystore tier.
sam: infra-bot reports a deploy to keystore cluster 03:20 UTC (rolling update): `keystore:1.12.0 -> 1.12.1`.
marie: customer says errors started ~03:45 so timeline aligns with that deploy.
olivia: theory: new image introduced a regression in connection pooling or health checks causing thundering connections when many auth requests arrive.
olivia: repro plan: 1) hit hosted inference gateway with a synthetic workload that triggers auth token creation at high rate (no cache). 2) measure keystore pod error rates and latencies. 3) confirm SDK retry amplification.
raj: spinning up a small load generator on canary infra to reproduce. using ab/hey to send 200 concurrent short generate calls with unique session ids.
marie: customer also noted that setting SDK cache TTL to 30s helps reduce errors on their side — suggests token churn is high.
olivia: temporary mitigation: enable auth caching flag at edge to prefer cached tokens for 60s. patching feature flag now.
sam: would prefer to rollback `keystore:1.12.1` if repro shows regression. starting rollback playbook readiness.
raj: initial canary run shows keystore pod CPU spikes + many `dial tcp` timeouts, matching customer. reproduces 503 fanout at gateway.
olivia: capturing heap and connection stats from keystore pods. also enabling additional keystore logs: `keystore.conn_pool.debug=true`.
marie: I need to update AcmeCorp — propose: short note that we're investigating, we've identified keystore-related regressions post-deploy, temporary mitigation applied (auth caching) and rollback readiness. ETA for update 30m. ok?
kevin: ok go ahead, add that we may roll back if instability persists.
raj: pre-rollback checklist: cordon new nodes, scale keystore replicas up by 2, and then roll back image on suspicious subset.
olivia: note for postmortem: add SDK retry behavior — many SDKs use aggressive immediate retries which amplify backend overload. recommend client-side backoff knob in next SDK release.
marie: message sent to customer: "We're investigating 503s tied to our keystore cluster after a recent deploy. Temporary caching mitigation in place, rollback on standby, will update in 30m. Apologies for the disruption. (correlation 3f2a1b)"
kevin: customer responded: thanks, they're seeing fewer 503s already but some residual failures remain.
raj: starting rollback now on one availability zone to verify stability before doing full rollback.
infra-bot: DeployManager: rollback of keystore image to 1.12.0 initiated at 03:57 UTC (task id d-8832).
raj: after rolling back AZ-a subset, keystore error rate dropped to baseline and gateway 503s fell by ~90% in the canary region.
olivia: greenlight to continue full rollback. proceeding.
sam: monitoring billing/usage spikes; need to track any double billing due to SDK retries — flagged billing team to watch for anomalies.
marie: final customer update sent: "We've reverted a recent keystore change which reduced the 503s. We'll follow up with a root cause and postmortem. Please open a support ticket if you see continued errors."
kevin: customer replied: closing for now, will reopen if issues return. :thumbsup:
marie: follow-ups: create incident postmortem, add SDK backoff recommendation, add deploy gating for keystore (smoke test auth QPS), and run a canary load test as part of CI.
olivia: filing a PR for the SDK backoff docs and a keystore smoke test template.
raj: adding runbook entry: detect keystore thundering pattern (conn timeouts + pod CPU spike) => auto-scale + rollback signal.
marie: thanks team. marking thread resolved but leaving postmortem tickets open."
